newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle off $1-$2 at $67-$68 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle off $1-$2 at $67-$68 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow Monday, with sales at $67.00 to $68.00 per cwt, down $1.00 to $2.00 from last sales Thursday, according to feedlot sources and USDA.
About 4,000 head traded in Kansas at $67.00-$68.00, mostly $68.00 for choice cattle, they said. About 1,000 to 2,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma areas.

Pressure was exerted by Friday's USDA monthly Cattle-On-Feed Report, which showed feedlot supplies at 101 percent of a year ago on November 1 and October placements on feed running at 111 percent, both above analysts' projections.

Prospects for increased numbers of market-ready cattle during the winter months was already starting to weigh on fed cattle prices, market sources said. Prices this fall were underpinned by tight finished supplies and marketing of cattle 20 to 30 days ahead of schedule.
Demand for cattle this week also was expected to run light, with beef usage seen soft because of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday.
Beef demand was expected to improve in the weeks between Thanksgiving and Christmas as retailers feature beef between heavy promotions of turkey and ham, market sources said.
